name: ZAP70 deficiency
aliases: combined immunodeficiency with normal CD4 and absent CD8

reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: A combined immunodeficiency that typically presents in infancy with recurrent and opportunistic infection despite a normal or even elevated total lymphocyte count
The signature immunophenotype is a selective absence of CD8 T cells with normal numbers of CD4 T cells that are nonetheless functionally defective
The circulating CD4 T cells fail to proliferate or respond to T-cell-receptor stimulation, so the defect is functional as well as numerical
Because it can present with a normal lymphocyte count, it may be missed on newborn TREC screening in some cases and requires flow-cytometric confirmation
B-cell numbers are usually normal but antibody responses are impaired owing to the lack of effective T-cell help
Autoimmune and immune dysregulatory features, including eczema and autoimmune cytopenias, can occur
Inheritance is autosomal recessive from biallelic loss-of-function variants in ZAP70
Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is curative and is the definitive treatment
reference.pathophysiology: ZAP70 (zeta-chain associated protein kinase of 70 kDa) is a tyrosine kinase that couples the engaged T-cell receptor to downstream signalling and is essential for the positive selection of thymocytes. Its deficiency blocks the selection and export of CD8 single-positive T cells, so peripheral CD8 cells are essentially absent, while CD4 T cells are selected and reach the circulation in normal numbers but cannot signal properly through the receptor and are therefore non-functional. The absent cytotoxic compartment and the functionally paralysed CD4 cells together produce a combined immunodeficiency with impaired cellular immunity and, through defective T-cell help, poor antibody responses.
additionalDifferentials: Severe combined immunodeficiency of other genotype
MHC class I deficiency (TAP defects) causing CD8 lymphopenia
Other T-cell receptor signalling defects (e.g. LCK, CD3 chain defects)
additionalInvestigations: Lymphocyte subsets showing absent CD8 T cells with normal CD4 counts
Lymphocyte proliferation assays to mitogens and antigens demonstrating poor responses
Flow cytometry or western blot for ZAP70 protein expression
Serum immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses
T-cell receptor excision circle (TREC) newborn screening result
ZAP70 gene sequencing for biallelic loss-of-function variants
redFlags: Opportunistic infection such as Pneumocystis pneumonia in an infant with a normal lymphocyte count
Failure to thrive with persistent or severe infection
Signs of graft-versus-host disease from non-irradiated blood products
reference.prognosis: Without treatment the condition is fatal in early childhood from infection, but allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, particularly when performed early, is curative and offers an excellent chance of long-term immune reconstitution.
pitfalls: Being falsely reassured by a normal total lymphocyte count and not measuring subsets
Overlooking the functional CD4 defect because CD4 numbers appear normal
Confusing the CD8 lymphopenia with an MHC class I (TAP) defect without protein or genetic testing
Giving live vaccines or non-irradiated blood products before diagnosis
references: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders in Infants and Children
IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
management: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the definitive curative therapy and should be undertaken early, before infective damage accrues
Give anti-infective prophylaxis with co-trimoxazole against Pneumocystis plus antifungal and antiviral cover, and treat intercurrent infections aggressively
Provide immunoglobulin replacement therapy for the impaired antibody responses
Avoid live vaccines and use only irradiated, CMV-safe, leucodepleted blood products to prevent transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease
Manage immune-dysregulatory features such as eczema and autoimmune cytopenias
Monitor for infection and growth and, around transplantation, immune reconstitution
Offer genetic counselling and family testing for the biallelic ZAP70 loss-of-function variants, with carrier and prenatal options
Refer promptly to a specialist immunology and transplant centre
